# Pi ProofKit — llms.txt
# Portable proof packs with offline verification: claims + evidence + a
# reproducible sha256 over a fully-specified canonical form.

> A bare number cannot be checked. A signed number requires trusting a signer.
> A proof pack can be checked by anyone, because it ships the exact bytes hashed.

## What it is
- read-only, zero-dependency, Node (ESM)
- lib.mjs: canonical form, claim kinds, validation, boundaries (imports nothing)
- pack.mjs: buildPack / verifyPack / renderPack / renderVerification (offline)
- proofkit-cli.mjs: --example --build --verify --canonical --hash --boundaries
- fixtures.mjs: the worked example pack
- test/proofkit.test.mjs: offline invariants, incl. a pin of the canonical form

## The one thing to remember
A digest proves INTEGRITY, not TRUTH.
- passing => the bytes are UNALTERED since the digest was taken (nothing more)
- it does NOT mean the claims are correct, complete, or well-founded
- to judge a claim you must read its basis and its evidence

## Canonical form (fully specified)
line  = {key}|{kind}|{value}|{basis}
lines = joined by "\n", pack order, NO trailing newline
null  = the literal four characters "null"
input = UTF-8 bytes (no BOM), hashed with sha256, rendered lowercase hex
not hashed: the digest itself, the label, and the evidence blob

## Anatomy
- scope:     endpoint, tool, version, measuredAt  (a pack is SCOPED, never universal)
- claims:    key | kind | value | basis           (inside the digest)
- evidence:  how to reach a value (cmd/URL)       (NOT inside the digest)
- canonical: the exact bytes + their sha256       (the thing you hash yourself)

## Claim kinds
measured (basis REQUIRED) | documented | derived | asserted (weakest) | not-claimed
A measured claim with no basis is REFUSED at build time.
A value/basis containing "|" or a newline is REFUSED (ambiguous form).
Duplicate keys are REFUSED.

## Verification: three verdicts, kept apart
intact   recomputed == recorded;  bytes unaltered        exit 0
tampered recomputed != recorded;  pack was altered       exit 1
invalid  pack malformed;          NO conclusion          exit 2
changing a BASIS alone      -> tampered (basis is hashed)
changing EVIDENCE alone     -> intact   (evidence is referenced, not hashed)
reordering claims           -> tampered (order is significant)

## Verified by an independent tool
example pack digest: 1e94219c8f934921edfdab37ed06f4b2874fe5830d86d67d7d702c8385a04876
PowerShell's own SHA256 over the same canonical bytes produced the same string.

## Example pack (measured 2026-10-19, node 28.0.1, protocol 28)
network.passphrase measured "Pi Testnet"
node.version       measured "28.0.1"
protocol.version   measured 28
events.pageCap     measured 100
ledger.retentionWindow measured 120960
ledger.retentionDays   derived  7
endLedger.exclusive    measured true
mainnet.sorobanRpc.reachable measured false

## Usage
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --example [--json]
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --build claims.json [--json]
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --verify pack.json [--json]     (exit 0/1/2)
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --canonical claims.json         (bytes to hash yourself)
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --hash somefile.txt
- node proofkit-cli.mjs --boundaries

## Not claimed
- that a passing verification proves the claims are true
- that a claim is complete, or that no other claim exists
- that a pack holds at another endpoint, version or time
- that the author is authenticated (a digest is not a signature)
- that the evidence's CONTENT is covered by the digest
- that Pi Network has adopted, reviewed or endorsed this
